documents: Yáñez-Cuadra et al. (2022), Interplate coupling and seismic potential in the Atacama Seismic Gap (Chile): Dismissing a rigid Andean sliver, Geophysical Research Letters 49, e2022GL098257 (published PDF, 13 pp.; supporting information not supplied)
pages_convention: printed journal pages (article pages '1 of 13' to '13 of 13', identical to PDF pages counted from 1)

entry.evidence: Modeling interseismic deformation is challenging, as it involves interplate coupling and often ignores continental internal deformation processes.

steps.action: States the aim: understand the processes that control interseismic strain accumulation along the Chilean margin, focusing on the Atacama seismic gap.
steps.quote: This study aims to better understand the underlying physical processes responsible for strain accumulation along the Chilean margin.

steps.action: Sets the published rival (back-slip plus a rigid Andean microplate or sliver, from Brooks 2003 onward) against their alternative: back-slip plus regional crustal strain and rigid motion.
steps.quote: In contrast, we represent surface velocities by incorporating crustal strain, in addition to standard rigid block motion and interplate coupling.

steps.action: Compiles published secular horizontal velocities from 104 GNSS stations (Métois et al. 2014; Klein, Meneses, et al. 2018) and transforms them to a stable South American frame.
steps.quote: We compiled a database of observed crustal secular horizontal velocities inferred from data of 104 GNSS stations

steps.action: Builds the forward model: Slab 2.0 triangulated back-slip model in a layered elastic half-space (EDKS), a linear regional velocity-gradient model (translation, rotation, strain), prediction-uncertainty covariance, and spatially variable EPIC Tikhonov regularization.
steps.quote: Here, we aim to model surface motion signals of regional extent that are not represented by the back-slip model

steps.action: Designs the model comparison: coupling is also estimated for back-slip plus a rigid Andean microplate and for back-slip alone, and the three models are ranked by Bayesian evidence (ABIC).
steps.quote: For comparison purposes, we perform coupling estimates for two additional interseismic strain accumulation models

steps.action: Runs least-squares inversions over σt from 3 to 15 mm/yr and β from 0.1 to 0.4, and selects the regularization parameters by maximum evidence with a coupling cap of 1+σt/vp.
steps.quote: Their best values are chosen as those that maximize the evidence

steps.action: Compares the evidence and ABIC of the three models; the regional-strain model scores best (σt = 6.4 mm/yr, β = 0.35).
steps.quote: our model incorporating surface regional strain consistently obtains the largest evidence values and minimum ABIC

steps.action: Rejects the back-slip-only and back-slip plus rigid-microplate models in favour of the model with regional strain.
steps.quote: Thus, we select our model as the most suitable among the three analyzed.

steps.action: Checks the fit of the preferred model: reduced chi-squared 1.27, mostly incoherent residuals with some locally coherent groups, and a trade-off between regional motion and coupling degree.
steps.quote: The misfit residuals have a reduced chi-squared of 1.27.

steps.action: Tests the stability of the inversion with two synthetic data sets (the preferred model's predictions and a checkerboard back-slip), each with Gaussian noise based on the observational uncertainties; the results are in the supplement (Figures S11, S16).
steps.quote: We demonstrate the stability and robustness of our results by performing two additional joint inversions constrained by synthetic data.

steps.action: Infers the coupling distribution: full coupling at 0–30 km depth, decreasing at depth, and five along-strike segments (Antofagasta HCZ, Taltal HCZ, Barranquilla LCZ, Chañaral PCZ, La Serena LCZ); resolution is given as σc = 0.096 and posterior correlation lengths.
steps.quote: we identify a latitudinal segmentation of coupling characterized by five along strike regions

steps.action: Infers the regional motion parameters: rigid rotation of 8.7e-7 ± 1.9e-7 °/yr, small translations, principal extension of 6.48e-8 parallel to convergence, and Wk = 0.166.
steps.quote: We find a counterclockwise rigid rotation rate of

steps.action: Compares the inferred rigid rotation and translation with the secular velocity uncertainties and finds them negligible; the regional motion is strain-dominated.
steps.quote: inferred rigid rotation and translation rates are negligible, as they represent only a fraction of the secular velocity uncertainties

steps.action: Sets the coupling segmentation against published slab-geometry, seismicity and historical-rupture results (Maksymowicz 2018; Tocopilla 2007; 1922 rupture extent) and infers a depth segmentation above the 1995 rupture and a possible La Serena barrier.
steps.quote: Our findings are consistent with a possible continuation of the sharp dip angle change across the Antofagasta HCZ segment.

steps.action: Compares the coupling model with earlier coupling models of the same region: along-strike similarity overall, but the Taltal LCZ is not recovered; the difference is attributed to method.
steps.quote: we do not infer the Taltal LCZ anomaly proposed as seismic barrier by Klein, Meneses, et al. (2018) and Molina et al. (2020)

steps.action: Estimates the slip deficit accumulated since 1922 (up to ~6.5 m) and the equivalent magnitudes for three segments (Mw 7.9, 8.4, 8.1).
steps.quote: we estimate a maximum slip deficit of ∼6.5 m accumulated since 1922 for the fully coupled portions of the megathrust

steps.action: Compares coupling with the 2014–2016 Copiapó slow slip event, the 2020 sequence and its afterslip, and subducting ridges and fracture zones; the SSE lies in a partially coupled zone, and correlations with the bathymetric features are mixed.
steps.quote: In contrast, our modeling shows that the SSE occurs in a partially coupled (∼0.6) zone

steps.action: Compares the coupling depth pattern and the regional strain with published viscoelastic models (Li 2015; Shi 2020), the expectation of non-Eulerian orogen deformation (Bird 2003), and fore-arc extensional tectonics.
steps.quote: Thus, suggesting that our estimates of regional strain rates are representative of those of a viscoelastic mantle model.

steps.action: Keeps mantle-wedge viscoelastic relaxation as the dominant source of the regional strain, over additional crustal shortening, because the inferred strain is extensional; the rigid sliver is dismissed.
steps.quote: we believe the latter process dominates due to the extensional nature of inferred strain rates

steps.action: Attributes the locally coherent residuals to neglected auxiliaries (non-uniform upper-plate compliance, lateral variations in elastic properties) rather than to the model itself.
steps.quote: This finding reveals a possible explanation for the local coherency of the misfit residuals observed in subgroups of GNSS stations.

steps.action: Concludes with an improved coupling model, a depth-dependent segmentation above the 1995 rupture, and strain-dominated regional motion consistent with fore-arc extension.
steps.quote: We apply this new methodology, along with recent developments in inversion techniques, and obtain an improved coupling model for the Atacama Region.

end.claim: Between 23° and 30°S, upper-plate surface motion is dominated by extensional regional strain with negligible rigid motion, so the rigid Andean sliver assumed in earlier coupling models is not needed; the strain model is best by Bayesian evidence among the three tested.

decisive_move.sentence: Adding a regional velocity-gradient (strain plus rigid motion) term to the back-slip inversion is what allowed rigid motion to be estimated as negligible and the strain model to win the evidence comparison.

gates.evidence: Action: the GNSS velocities are compiled from published studies (p. 3), so no hypothesis directed data acquisition. Claim: the strain model could have lost the evidence comparison to the back-slip-only and rigid-sliver models (p. 5), and the rigid terms could have been significant (p. 7). Synthetic tests are reported only in the supplement. Registration: the regularization parameters and the coupling cap were chosen on the same data (p. 5); nothing is said to have been fixed beforehand.

imports.item: Bayesian evidence and Akaike Bayesian Information Criterion (ABIC) for model and regularization selection
Tikhonov regularization in the EPIC spatially variable form, with generalized least squares
rate-and-state and slip-rate-dependent friction as an interpretive frame for SSEs

novelty_claims.quote: [...] novel methodology to jointly estimate interplate coupling along with upper plate rigid motion and surface strain
We present a novel interseismic strain accumulation model of the subduction interface for the Atacama Seismic Gap
[...] this study we develop a novel methodology to model interseismic strain accumulation in subduction zones

limits: Headline claim (rigid sliver not needed; strain-dominated motion), coded as contradicted with status best_explanation. Sub-claims and their statuses: the coupling distribution and five-segment segmentation, estimate_with_resolution (σc = 0.096, correlation lengths, p. 7); slip-deficit magnitudes Mw 7.9/8.4/8.1, estimate_with_resolution, with an unknown start of accumulation for the 1995 segment (p. 9); depth-dependent segmentation above the 1995 rupture, best_explanation by consistency with published slab geometry (p. 7); viscoelastic relaxation as the source of the regional strain, best_explanation stated as belief, with no viscoelastic model run (p. 10). The evidence values, the synthetic and checkerboard test results, and the parameter-selection curves are only in the supplement, which was not supplied, so their outcomes cannot be checked here. The data are reused from Métois et al. (2014) and Klein, Meneses, et al. (2018), so the comparison with those groups' coupling models is the same data analysed by a different method; the Taltal LCZ disagreement is attributed to method without an ablation that isolates which difference (strain term, prediction uncertainty, or EPIC) causes it. Resolution near the trench and at Taltal Ridge is low, so smaller low-coupling features could be concealed (pp. 7, 9). The v_checks entry coded as replication (consistency with independent SSE, afterslip and geophysical results) is a loose fit to the NASEM category: the coder's inference is that these data address related but not identical questions. No review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded. Composition is none_fits: the walk is method-led estimation with one model-selection step among three rivals; strong_inference is the closest category, but the evidence comparison is a fit-and-parsimony ranking, not a crucial test with distinct predicted outcomes.

disagreements.target: Rigid Andean microplate / sliver model (Brooks et al. 2003; Chlieh et al. 2011; Klein, Meneses, et al. 2018; Métois [...]
disagreements.support: Evidence and ABIC favour back-slip plus regional strain over back-slip plus rigid microplate, and the jointly inferred rigid rotation and translation fall within the velocity uncertainties.
disagreements.quote: we show that surface motion is dominated by strain, with rather negligible rigid motion, dismissing the rigid Andean microplate model typically assumed in previous studies

disagreements.target: Taltal LCZ barrier proposed by Klein, Meneses, et al. (2018) and Molina et al. (2020)
disagreements.support: Their coupling inversion of largely the same GNSS data does not recover a low-coupling zone at Taltal; they attribute the difference to their strain term, epistemic uncertainties and EPIC regularization, while noting low resolution there.
disagreements.quote: we do not infer the Taltal LCZ anomaly proposed as seismic barrier by Klein, Meneses, et al. (2018) and Molina et al. (2020)

disagreements.target: Klein, Duputel, et al. (2018) association of the Copiapó SSE with very low coupling
disagreements.support: Their model places the SSE in a partially coupled (~0.6) zone, and the predicted 4-year slip budget (15.8 cm, Mw ~6.92) matches the event.
disagreements.quote: Klein, Duputel, et al. (2018) associates this SSE with very low (<0.2) megathrust coupling, without accounting for the slip budget released [...] .

disagreements.target: Studies linking subducting ridges and fracture zones to coupling segmentation (Contreras-Reyes & Carrizo 2011; Molina et al. 2020; Métois et [...]
disagreements.support: Fracture zones correlate with segment limits, but the Taltal and Copiapó ridges relate oppositely to coupling (one fully coupled, one below 0.7), with a resolution caveat at Taltal.
disagreements.quote: However, the Taltal and Copiapo Ridges have an opposite relation with our coupling inferences.
